title.narrative: Health emergency response to the Sudanese refugees influx in Libya

description.narrative: Sudan is the world’s largest displacement crisis, with the staggering number of 10 million people forcibly displaced and 14 areas at risk of famine. The dimension of this crisis has devastating effects on neighboring countries, which are also plagued with instability, violence and human rights abuses. The influx into Libya is more apparent, but not limited to, AlKufra, which has a local population of 61,000 people.Since April 2023, UNHCR has registered 21,503 newly arrived Sudanese in Tripoli. However, in 2024 only, AlKufra health authorities have issued 49,177 health certificates to newly arrived Sudanese. WHO recently conducted several field visits in AlKufra, finding that Sudanese refugees were settling in about 51 rural collective shelters, and in governmental buildings. AlKufra has one general hospital, 13 partially functioning primary healthcare centers, one Mental Health center, one center for Diabetes and Endocrinology Treatment and a branch of the National Center for Disease Control. The local health authorities have reported severe shortage of essential medicines, and the elective surgeries have been suspended due to lack of anesthesia. One refugee died of TB on 24 June and 50 more cases have been reported.Through this allocation, WHO will leverage its privileged relationship with the national and local health authorities and access to:1. Strengthen the existing health system to expand access to lifesaving and life-sustaining health services to Sudanese refugees and hosting communities. 2. Deploy mobile clinics to enable access to life-saving services in hard-to-reach areas and within the settlements. 3. Provide mental health and psychosocial support to refugees, with a priority for women and girls and GBV survivors. 4. Ensure screening and management of medical complications associated with Severe Acute Malnutrition. 5. Scale up disease surveillance and rapid response.6. Ensure effective inter-sector coordination.As Health Sub-Sector lead, WHO has convened a meeting with all agencies to clarify the exact scope and location of each agency's activities. Please refer to Annex 1 to see the overall activity mapping, and clarifications on how agencies will avoid overlapping.
